newsitem.title: USA: Speigel profits lower on poor catalog performace.
newsitem.headline: Speigel profits lower on poor catalog performace.

text.p: Speciality retailer Spiegel Inc. posted sharply lower fourth-quarter profits, blaming poor performance in its mail-order business.

The company, best known for its Spiegel Catalogue and Eddie Bauer clothing stores, earned $19.8 million, or 18 cents a share, for the fourth quarter, compared with profits of $37.4 million, or 35 cents a share, for the year-ago period.
Revenues were $1.09 billion vs. $1.12 billion in the 1995 quarter.
"Overall, our fourth-quarter and full-year results were disappointing," said Spiegel Chief Executive John Shea. "However, the performance was mixed by division."
Shea said Eddie Bauer achieved record results, but the Spiegel Catalogue and Newport News catalogue were hurt by tightened credit policies and lower productivity from catalogue mailings.
The continued industrywide trend toward higher charge-offs, particularly bankruptcies, was also a factor.

Margins at Eddie Bauer improved significantly due to lower markdowns from improved promotional strategies and inventory planning. Margins for Spiegel Catalogue fell as the company cut prices on merchandise that no longer fit the overall catalogue.
Spiegel said it had cut inventories by 12 percent by the end of the yeard despite opening 32 new Eddie Bauer stores.
The Downers Grove, Ill.-based company said it reduced its total debt to $340 million by the end of 1996.
Spiegel said it's Spiegel Catalogue will put into effect new strategies to regain market share in the coming year and said it plans to open 70 new Eddie Bauer stores in North America.
Spiegel sells fashionable apparel and home furnishings through catalogues, more than 450 speciality retail stores and through electronic shopping.
Spiegel stock dropped 37.5 cents to $6.75 in early afternoon trading on the Nasdaq market.
